title: SSoR shared definitions
$comment: Roadmap item 2 draft material. Companion to spec/boundary-0.1-draft.md. Origin and record time are assigned by admission and are readOnly: a payload that carries them for its own claims is stripped or rejected (boundary rules B-07, B-15).

origin.description: Assigned at admission from authenticated identity and the authority map. NEVER taken from the payload (B-07).

validTime.description: When the claim says it held in the world. A claim that later proves false still has a valid time (B-16).

to.description: Open-ended when the claim is still in force.

recordTime.description: When SSoR recorded the item — not when the world learned it (B-17). Server-assigned.

supersession.description: Records are never edited in place. A correction is a new record that supersedes the old one; the superseded record stays, marked (B-06, B-18). Set by admission/adjudication, not by the original submitter.

supersedes.description: Ids of the claims this record supersedes (correction) — distinct from resolution, which supersedes nothing (B-19).

reason.description: Why the earlier claim was wrong or is being replaced.

provenance.description: Required when a model produced the item; admission verifies what it can (README §Admission: which model, from which inputs).

inputs.description: References to the episodes, receipts or records the model read. Lineage must terminate in something checkable (issue #3).

prompt.description: Optional prompt/template reference (not raw content) for re-runs.

confidence.description: Stored as metadata only. NOT a calibrated probability and NEVER affects origin (README §Origin rules).

audience.description: Principals permitted to see the record. Governance comes before retrieval: enforced on every surface before search or return (README §5).

source.description: CloudEvents source — with 'id', the deduplication key (B-14).

id.description: CloudEvents id — with 'source', the deduplication key (B-14).
